The governor who oversaw the Vatican City State (the location that houses St. Peter’s Basilica, which is dedicated to the same saint as Leeds Minster) was **Camillo Serafini**. His tenure ended with his death on **21 March 1952**.

> *Camillo Serafini (died 21 March 1952) was the last Governor of the Vatican City State – his death brought the office to an end.*  
> – Wikipedia “Governor of the Vatican City State”

   Camillo Serafini served from the establishment of the Vatican City State in 1929 until his death.
3. **End of Tenure** – His service ended when he passed away on **21 March 1952**, which is the terminating date for both the governor’s term and, chronologically, the city’s first governor‑person in that position.

*(The head of the Catholic Church—i.e., the Pope—continued to serve after this date; the question specifically asks for the governor’s end date, so the relevant date is 21 March 1952.)*
